requirement:
Each attachment's `span` is a half-open byte range in the original file
snapshot, even when the caller has selected a nested item. Slicing that
snapshot at the span yields the complete source construct, including its
delimiters. Repeated occurrences have their own spans.
rationale:
The reviewed tests cover each obligation in `requirements.sdk.outlines.attachments.span`.

**Byte range in the original snapshot, even for a nested selection.**
- `crates/trust-but-verify/tests/outline_content.rs#fn[rust_attachments_keep_the_owner_kind_and_original_bytes]` selects `mod[m]/fn[f]`, which sits deep inside the file.
- It slices the original `source` with every returned `a.span` and asserts the exact text. The items returned include the file-level `//! file docs`, which lies outside the selected item. Spans relative to the selection would fail this.
- The source contains `é` in `café`, so the byte offsets are checked against multi-byte text.

**Complete construct including delimiters.**
- `fn[bundled_languages_classify_only_their_attachment_syntax]` asserts full slices for many forms:
  - Rust `/*! inner */`, `/** outer */` and `/* ordinary */`.
  - Multi-line Python decorator `@pkg.decorate(\n  1\n)`, which is also checked on the `class[C]` item.
  - Markdown `<!-- multi\nline -->`.
  - TypeScript `@dec`, plus line comments across languages.
- The assertions use `trim_end()`. The requirement does not call for a trailing newline, so this does not hide a requirement-relevant difference.

**Half-open range.**
- `fn[custom_attachment_spans_are_checked_against_the_original_snapshot]` uses `Span::new(1, 3)` over `_é_`. The slice is exactly `é`, so the end is exclusive.
- It also rejects spans that split a character, spans past the snapshot, and spans that extend past the item.

**Repeated occurrences have their own spans.**
- The Rust test has two identical `/// café` comments. It asserts both with their text and that the first span ends at or before the second begins.
- The Python test has two decorators.
- The TOML test has multiple `#` comments.

The tests are marked `{test}` for the subject, so there is no marking gap.
